faq.a: Rajabu is associated with the Arabic form رَجَبُ, whose core sense is rajabu; the month of rajab (swahili form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Rajabu?
faq.a: Rajabu is associated with Arabic. Rajabu is the Swahili form of Arabic رَجَب (Rajab), the name of a lunar month, used as a male given name.
Yes — the underlying form رَجَبُ is Arabic.
Rajabu can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Rajabu should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Rajab is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Rajabu mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Rajabu is rendered رجب and carries the sense رجب، رجب کا مہینہ.

faq.q: What does Rajabu mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Rajabu is rendered رجب and carries the sense رجب، ماه رجب.
A romanized syllable approximation is ra-ja-bu. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Rajabu?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Rajabu, rajabu. Script forms are رجب, رَجَبُ, रजब.

faq.q: Is Rajabu a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
